title: When is a linear optimal power flow safe to dispatch from, and which cheap AC repair makes it safe?
lede: research programme on linear OPF dispatch feasibility on the PGLib-OPF benchmark: the DC dispatch overloads branches on all 11 congested cases; a trust-region successive linearisation of the AC power flow repairs 7 of 11 at the AC optimum's cost, and on 12 held-out angle-limited (SAD) cases the same rules with linearised angle rows repair 7 of 11 (angle-blind: 3); at the AC optimum's voltage schedule (an oracle). Without it, at the case file's 1.0 pu setpoints, the repair clears 2 of 11 API and 2 of 11 SAD cases and none meets voltage and Q limits; a repair that moves voltage setpoints with P, with a small margin inside every limit, is fully feasible on 28 of 34 cases from that start at 0.17 to 0.34 % mean cost above the AC optimum (tuned on those cases; held-out test next); analytic Jacobian sensitivities give the same counts (29 of 34) with 2 power flows per round, but the QP, not the power flows, sets the run time; an audit of all 347 QPs against Clarabel finds PIPS failing on 26 solvable elastic QPs, and with Clarabel the repair is fully feasible on 21 of 34 (31 with the voltage stage) about 5x faster; LPAC-C, the linear model with voltage and reactive power, run one-shot, is fully feasible on 0 of 34 and has no solution on 9 (7 SAD); on 244 load-perturbed copies (each bus x 0.9 to 1.1) the repair is fully feasible on 0.66 (95 % interval 0.52 to 0.79) and 0.91 with the voltage stage, matching the one-load-point counts, though 101 of 360 copies (71 of 120 congested) have no AC optimum; traced with 30 rounds instead of 10, the repair alone is fully feasible on 31 of 34 (late finishers +0.41 % over the AC optimum), its misses are mostly curvature on thermal and Q rows, and the programme's convergence bound as written is refuted (one case stalls at local infeasibility); on 24 held-out cases of 500 to 2,000 buses the frozen repair is never feasible within 10 rounds (0 of 12 scorable), refuting H2 as written, and feasible on 6 of 12 within 20 rounds, 8 of 12 with the voltage stage.
summary: An open research programme (opened 2026-11-12, track 21) on whether the dispatch from a linear optimal power flow, the model markets clear energy with, is feasible once the AC physics is applied, and how many AC power flows a repair needs to make it so at the AC optimum's cost. Benchmark: PGLib-OPF v23.07 (typical, congested API and small-angle-difference SAD sets of 12 cases, 14 to 300 buses), solved with PYPOWER, whose AC optima match the library's published values within 0.005 %. So far (experiments in infra-dcopf): the plain DC dispatch overloads branches on all 11 API cases with an AC optimum; a trust-region successive linearisation (finite-difference loss factors and flow sensitivities, a QP, an elastic l1 fallback) repairs 7 of 11 at the optimum's cost, with rules set on those cases; on the 12 SAD cases, held out, the same rules plus linearised angle-difference rows repair 7 of the 11 with an AC optimum, while the angle-blind version repairs 3 and lands 6.5–17.6 % below the optimum's cost by breaking up to 16 angle limits. Milestone 3 (2026-11-12): without that oracle schedule, at PGLib's own 1.0 pu setpoints, the same repair clears thermal, slack and angle limits on 2 of 11 API and 2 of 11 SAD cases (6 and 7 with it), none of its dispatches meets voltage and Q limits, and an AC OPF over voltages only after it makes 16 of 34 cases fully feasible at a mean 0.8–4.3 % above the optimum's cost. Milestone 3b (2026-11-12): a successive linearisation over P and the generator voltage setpoints, with voltage and Q limits as linear rows, is fully feasible on only 5 of 34 cases as pre-registered (it stops within 0.1 % of the limits on 19); with a small margin inside every limit (a variant chosen after that result) it is fully feasible on 18 of 34, and on 28 of 34 with the voltage-only stage after it, at a mean 0.17–0.34 % above the AC optimum's cost; not yet tested on held-out cases. Milestone 2 (2026-11-13): the same sensitivities from the power-flow Jacobian (one sparse solve per round, matching central differences to 1.3×10−5) give 19 and 29 of 34, so the counts do not hang on finite-difference noise; the run time falls only 1.1× because the QP takes 98–99 % of it, and a finished repair's cost moves by up to 3.1 points with the derivative source, since the method stops at its first feasible round. Milestone 2b (2026-11-13): every QP the repair poses (347) re-solved by Clarabel as a referee: where PIPS reports a solution it is the right one (objectives agree within 10−6), but PIPS fails on 36 of 99 elastic QPs, 26 of them solvable; with Clarabel on every QP the repair is fully feasible on 21 of 34 (31 with the voltage-only stage), loses no case, and runs about 5× faster. Milestone 4a (2026-11-13): LPAC-C (Coffrin and Van Hentenryck 2014, PowerModels' conic form), solved once and run through one AC power flow, is fully feasible on 0 of 34 cases; it has no solution on 9 (7 of the 11 SAD cases; a second solver agrees on 8), and where it solves the AC power flow breaks Q limits on 21 of 25, with 376 of 1,000 generator voltage setpoints exactly on a bound. As a starting point for the repair it is about as good as the DC dispatch (17 against 15 fully feasible on the 25 cases it solves). On 244 load-perturbed copies (every bus’s load × 0.9 to 1.1, 10 seeds) the repair is fully feasible on 0.66 (95 % cluster bootstrap 0.52 to 0.79) and 0.91 with the voltage stage (0.83 to 0.97), its one-load-point verdict matches the copies’ majority on 30 of 34 cases, and it beats the voltage stage on the DC dispatch on 29 cases with no losses (P = 3.7e-9); 101 of 360 copies, 71 of 120 congested ones, have no AC optimum and are excluded. Milestone 7, empirical half (2026-11-13): traced round by round with a 30-round budget instead of 10, the repair alone is fully feasible on 31 of 34 cases (by round 20; 21 at 10 rounds), the ten late finishers at a mean +0.41 % over the AC optimum; 168 of 224 misses in rounds 1–10 are curvature failures (the step’s second-order error exceeds the margin, on thermal and Q rows), the one-step finishing condition holds on all 190 hard misses, and the convergence bound H4 as written is refuted (10× or more off on 25 of 31 finishers; case73 API stalls with a well-conditioned Jacobian at a point of local infeasibility). Limits: one AC solver, few congested copies with an AC optimum, no baseline yet from LPAC-W or optimised linearisations. Target: IEEE Transactions on Power Systems. Milestone 6 (2026-11-13): on the 24 held-out PGLib cases of 500 to 2,000 buses (12 scorable; PIPS has no AC optimum on 11), the frozen repair is fully feasible within 10 rounds on 0 of 12, refuting H2 as written; within a 20-round budget fixed beforehand on 6 of 12, and 8 of 12 with the voltage stage (DC dispatch with the same stage: 0), at a mean +0.66 % over the AC optimum.
